newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says forex relations with Japan "fine".
newsitem.headline: Rubin says forex relations with Japan "fine".

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Thursday that relations between Treasury and Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) were strong and that the two countries work well together when necessary on foreign exchange issues.
"If you ask me about our working relations with the MOF on foreign exchange matters, when appropriate, they're fine," Rubin told reporters after a ceremony at the Treasury.
"We have very good general relations with the MOF,"he added.

Rubin was asked by a reporter whether remarks made earlier this week by Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto suggested that cooperation between Japan and the United States on foreign exchange matters was not as strong as previously.

"The answer to your ... question is that we work very well with the (Japanese) Ministry of Finance," Rubin said. "And as we said in the statement, the G7 nations also are all committed to working together, when appropriate, with respect to foreign exchange matters."

Rubin was referring to the statement issued last weekend at the annual summit of the seven leading industrial nations -- the United States, Britain, Canada, Italy, Japan, France and Germany -- in which the leaders asked finance ministers to continue to cooperate closely in foreign exchange markets.

Last Monday, Hashimoto sent U.S. financial markets into a brief nosedive by seeming to suggest Japan might sell U.S. government bonds and buy gold if Washington did not cooperate with Tokyo to stabilize currency rates.

On Wednesday, Rubin played down that possibility by saying that he did not expect such sales and adding that he was confident U.S. markets could absorb them with only temporary disruption if they did occur.

"Our markets are so deep and so broad that even if there was enormous concerted selling by a foreign country -- I have no reason to think it would occur -- our markets could absorb it readily," Rubin told reporters.
